title: Regia Aeronautica original General Staff comparison of air strength, aircraft losses, personnel losses, and frontline unit commitment, June 1940 to September 1942
sourceAuthor: Basilio Di Martino, The Regia Aeronautica in September 1942, Nuova Antologia Militare 6(24), 2025, pp. 701 onwards
originalArchivalCitation: Italian Air Force Central Library / AUSMA, Monographs, b. 27, f. 18; original confidential Chief of Staff study circa August-September 1942, associated with Gen. Rino Corso Fougier
forceScope: Italian Regia Aeronautica core Armata Aerea; generally EXCLUDES attached Army/Navy auxiliary aviation (ESERCITAVIA/MARINAVIA), and 1940-41 Italian East African air force. Loss classes and front-line aircraft denominators are not necessarily identical.

unitFormationOperationalCommitment.commitmentFronts: multiple including Libya, Mediterranean and Italian metropolitan fronts

unitFormationOperationalCommitment.commandLimit: Sardinian, Sicilian, Libyan and Aegean commands counted in deployed numerator; denominator includes full force

ownAircraftLossesThrough1942August21.warning: 1,409 is a combined ground, irreparable damage and unknown/missing category; 715 is not all enemy-caused aircraft losses. About 1,000 transferred or decommissioned must not be counted again as crashes/destroyed; original rounds about 4,400.

cumulativePilotAndFlyingTechnicianCasual.warning: Died/KIA, missing and prisoner categories are combined in the original historical statement; not 1,243 pilot deaths and not 2,907 deaths. Excludes wounded, sick and other nonfatal removals. Date is approximate.

pilotsInFlyingUnitsSnapshots.note: The text separately refers to 103 fighter-equivalent squadriglie if 15 interceptor/night-fighter sections are included. The Sept15 aircraft/formation comparison and Sept20 pilot-squadron comparison are NOT the same exact date.

broaderOfficialAirForceComparison.warning: Modern service-level rounded all-aircraft summary, not the same restricted frontline bomber/fighter count or operational-readiness definition as the 1942 original report.
